cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "ensures",
 "proof_obligation": "bridge",
 "diagnosis": "lemma_all_small's postcondition contains a spurious conjunct '&& j != 0', which is false for j == 0 whenever q is nonempty (counterexample |q|=1, q[0]=-1, i=0). The preconditions only establish that every element is below i, so the ensures cannot be proved. The intended postcondition (mirroring lemma_all_big) is forall j :: 0<=j<|q| ==> q[j] < i. The InsertBST timeout is a consequence of relying on this flawed lemma contract in the x < i branch."}
EOF
sed -i '205s/q\[j\] < i && j != 0/q[j] < i/' program.dfy && sed -n 205p program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy

**What was wrong:** the postcondition (`ensures`) of `lemma_all_small` at line 205 had an extra condition, `&& j != 0`. That condition is false for the first element of any non-empty sequence, which is exactly the counterexample Dafny gave (`|q| = 1`, `q[0] = -1`, `i = 0`). The lemma's preconditions only say that every element is less than `i`, so the postcondition could never be proved.

**Fix:** I removed `&& j != 0`, so the line now reads `ensures forall j::0<=j < |q| ==> q[j] < i`. This matches the companion lemma `lemma_all_big`.

**The `InsertBST` timeout:** it went away with the same fix and needed no change of its own. Its `x < i` branch calls this lemma, and the false postcondition was likely what made that proof time out.
